desc: Derive and verify the symmetry argument: each unordered pair of distinct cells co-occurs in exactly C(mn-2, k-2) arrangements; corrected formula Σ d(L-d) = L(L²-1)/6 = C(L+1,3); hand-verified both examples (2,2,2)→8 and (1,4,3)→20.
Implement a helper `comb(N, r) mod p` using a multiplicative loop with modular inverse (r = k-2 ≤ 1e5, so O(r) is fine); handle edge cases (k=2 gives 1).
Implement the 1D distance-sum contribution `T(L) = L(L²-1) mod p` (division by 6 applied once at the end via precomputed inverse of 6).
Implement `distanceSum` as `comb(mn-2, k-2) × (n²·T(m) + m²·T(n)) × inv(6) mod p`, reducing values mod p at each step.
Test against brute-force enumeration for small grids (all m,n,k with mn ≤ 8) plus the provided examples (2,2,2)→8 and (1,4,3)→20 — all passed.
Review complexity (O(k) time, O(1) space) and finalize the solution within the starter code with explanatory comments.
